title: Cat With Tears of Joy Emoji 😹 Meaning and Uses
description: 😹 is the cat version of the laughing-crying face. Learn when it means real laughter, when it is mocking (like 🫵😹), and how it differs from 😂 and 💀.
summary: The 😹 cat with tears of joy emoji means laughing so hard you cry, shown as a cat. It works like 😂 with a cuter, sillier tone. In meme culture it has also become a mocking laugh, most famously in the pointing combo 🫵😹, used to ridicule someone.
meaning: At face value 😹 is simply 😂 for cat people. Something is hilarious, the sender is in tears, and the whiskers add charm. Cat owners use it for the ridiculous things their pets do, such as misjudged jumps and fights with their own tails. For years that was the whole story, and plenty of people still use it this way with complete sincerity.

Younger users gave it a second personality. As 😂 came to feel overused, alternatives took over, and 😹 was adopted for a particular flavor: laughing at someone. The cat's face looks more gleeful and less sympathetic than the human one, so it suits taunting. The pairing 🫵😹, a finger pointing at the viewer plus the laughing cat, became a standard reply for mocking a bad take, a failed brag, or a rival team's loss.

Because of that split, context decides how it lands. From a relative or a friend who adores cats, 😹 is warm laughter. Under a stranger's post, especially repeated or paired with the pointing finger, it is ridicule. The irony layer also means some people use it for humor that is deliberately lowbrow, treating the cat as a signal that the joke is dumb and they know it.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Among friends it is a friendly laugh with a goofy edge. It suits slapstick stories and self-inflicted mishaps. If your friend normally uses 💀 or 😭 for laughter and suddenly sends 😹, they are probably being playful or teasing you a little, since the cat has that meme association.

contexts.label: On TikTok and X
contexts.body: Here the mocking sense dominates. Comment sections fill with 🫵😹 when a creator is caught out or says something embarrassing. Sports fans use it after a rival loses. Meme pages attach it to low-quality, intentionally absurd edits. Sincere use still exists but is easy to mistake for trolling.

contexts.label: On pet accounts
contexts.body: Cat fail videos and blooper photos are captioned with 😹 in its original spirit. It tells viewers the clip is funny and that the laughter is affectionate. This is the context in which the emoji is most literal: a laughing reaction to a cat, rendered as a cat.

examples.text: He tried to jump on the counter and missed by a mile 😹
examples.meaning: Affectionate laughter at a cat's failed leap.

examples.text: You studied all night and the test got moved 🫵😹
examples.meaning: Teasing someone by pointing and laughing at their bad luck.

examples.text: I waved back at someone who wasn't waving at me 😹
examples.meaning: Laughing at one's own embarrassing moment.
Mocking a prediction the sender finds laughable.
The sender is laughing hard at what was just said.

examples.text: Grandma's cat stole the whole turkey leg 😹
examples.meaning: Sharing a funny family pet story.

combos.meaning: Pointing and laughing at someone; the best-known mocking use.
Either helpless laughter or exaggerated ridicule, depending on who it is aimed at.
Something so funny the sender is both crying and 'dead.'

confusedWith.difference: 😂 is the universal laughing face and reads as sincere, if a bit dated to younger users. 😹 expresses the same laugh but adds either cuteness or, in meme spaces, a jeering tone the human face lacks.
😸 is a happy grin with no tears, suited to mild amusement. 😹 has tears at the eyes and means full laughter, or laughter at someone's expense.
😿 has a single tear and a frown and means sadness. 😹 has tears from laughing and a wide open smile. At small sizes the two can be misread, so check the mouth.

avoid: Do not reply with it to someone's sincere post unless you intend to laugh at them, because many readers now take it as mockery.
Avoid it when a friend shares something embarrassing in confidence and needs reassurance, not laughter.
Skip the pointing combo with people outside your friend group, where it comes across as bullying.
design: A cat's head with eyes shut tight in laughter, a wide open grin, and a teardrop at the outer corner of each eye. Most vendors use yellow or orange fur and blue tears, closely matching their own 😂 design with ears and whiskers added. The layout is consistent across platforms.

faqs.a: It means 'look at you, that's laughable.' The pointing finger targets the reader and the cat laughs at them. It is used to mock, sometimes as friendly banter and sometimes as a real put-down in arguments and fan rivalries.
Not inherently. Used about a funny story or a pet, it is harmless. It becomes rude when directed at a person's mistake or opinion, where it implies they are a joke.

faqs.q: Why do people use 😹 instead of 😂?
faqs.a: Some simply like cats. Others find 😂 stale and want a laugh with more personality. In meme culture the cat is chosen on purpose because it looks sillier and more taunting.

faqs.q: What does 😹 mean from a girl or a guy?
faqs.a: They found something very funny. Whether they are laughing with you or at you depends on the message. If you just told a joke, it is a compliment. If you just made a claim, they may be teasing.
